slides.title: [Recursive] / splitting
slides.hook: Split on paragraphs first, then lines, then words. And why the defaults still cut sentences in half.
inside: Real LangChain outputs, good and bad
5 settings that change where it cuts
One splitter config with every fix

slides.title: Cut at the [seams]
slides.text: Documents already have structure. Recursive splitting tries the biggest separator first and falls back to a smaller one only when a piece is still too big.
slides.after: That's the default list in LangChain's `RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter`, which its docs call "the recommended one for generic text".

slides.title: How it [recurses]

steps: Take the first separator in the list that appears in the text.
Split any piece at or over `chunk_size` again, with the separators after it.
Merge pieces under the limit back together, up to `chunk_size`.
Start the next chunk with whole pieces from the end of the last, up to `chunk_overlap`.

slides.after: Overlap moves whole pieces. With sentence pieces and `chunk_size=100`, `chunk_overlap=50` repeats a 45-character sentence. `chunk_overlap=40` repeats nothing.

slides.title: The defaults still / [cut] sentences
slides.text: The default list has no sentence separator. A paragraph with no line breaks falls through to spaces, so cuts land wherever the characters run out.

visuals.caption: chunk_size=60, chunk_overlap=0, default separators
chunks: Refunds are accepted within 30 days of purchase. !!After 30!!
!!days,!! refunds need manager approval. !!Digital items are!!

slides.after: This is the chunk boundary problem. The approval rule is split across chunks 1 and 2, and chunk 3 says "never refundable." with no subject.

slides.title: Add a sentence / [separator]
slides.text: Put `". "` between lines and words. Then `keep_separator` decides which chunk the period lands in.

visuals.caption: Chunk 2 of the same paragraph, chunk_size=60

options.output: !!.!! After 30 days, refunds need manager approval
After 30 days, refunds need manager approval!!.!!
After 30 days, refunds need manager approval

slides.title: Keep the / [last resort]
slides.text: The final `""` splits into single characters, so no chunk can go over `chunk_size`. Remove it, and a piece with no separator left stays whole, however long.

visuals.label: Without `""`
visuals.verdict: 75 characters, over the limit of 40, and no warning

slides.after: Keep `""` so chunks fit your embedder's limit. Drop it only if long strings must stay whole, then check lengths.

slides.title: Size in [tokens]
slides.text: `chunk_size` counts characters by default, because `length_function=len`. The default 4,000 characters is roughly 1,000 tokens of English, and your embedder's limit is in tokens.
bullets: `model_name` picks the matching encoding: `cl100k_base` for text-embedding-3.
With no `model_name` or `encoding_name`, it falls back to the `"gpt2"` encoding.
For open models, `from_huggingface_tokenizer(tokenizer)` counts with the model's own tokenizer.

slides.title: Split Markdown / on [headings]
slides.text: `from_language()` has separator presets for 28 languages and formats in v1.1.3. For Markdown, headings come first.

visuals.label: Default separators, chunk_size=120 (shortened)
chunks:
## Refunds
Refunds are accepted within… approval.
!!## Shipping!!
visuals.verdict: The Shipping heading ends the refunds chunk

visuals.label: `from_language(Language.MARKDOWN)`
chunks:
## Refunds
Refunds are accepted within… approval.

!!## Shipping!!
Orders ship within 2 business days…
visuals.verdict: Each section keeps its own heading

slides.title: Put it all / [together]
slides.text: Every fix from this post in one splitter: a sentence separator, the period kept at the end, and sizes counted in your embedder's tokens.

visuals.code:
R = RecursiveCharacterTextSplitter
splitter = R.from_tiktoken_encoder(
    model_name="text-embedding-3-small",
    separators=["\n\n", "\n", ". ", " ", ""],
    keep_separator="end",
    chunk_size=500, chunk_overlap=100,
)

bullets: 500 and 100 are example sizes. Set `chunk_size` from your embedder's input limit.

cards.title: Use it when
items: Docs have structure: paragraphs, headings, lists
Ingest must be cheap: it makes no model calls
Every chunk must fit a hard token limit

cards.title: Move on when
items: Topics change mid-paragraph: try semantic chunking
Answers need the text around the match: try parent-document retrieval
Text has no reliable breaks, like raw OCR: cuts fall back to fixed-size

slides.title: [Cheat] sheet
rows: Biggest separator first, then smaller ones
Add `". "` before `" "` to cut between sentences
Keep `""` last so no chunk exceeds `chunk_size`

slides.title: [Semantic] / chunking
slides.line: Recursive splitting cuts where the text has breaks. Semantic chunking cuts where the meaning shifts.
